comment: The guidance elaborates a sound framework for interoperability and semantic governance of health data. However, it largely assumes that participating countries have a relatively complete existing digital health foundation. Many low- and middle-income countries face fragmented legacy systems, limited technical capacity, and weak data infrastructure, which makes the ideal full interoperability framework difficult to implement in one step. The guidance lacks a practical gradient implementation path for countries with weak foundational conditions, which may lead to the framework being shelved due to mismatched local conditions.

public.text: The guidance elaborates a sound framework for interoperability and semantic governance of health data. However, it largely assumes that participating countries have a relatively complete existing digital health foundation. Many low- and middle-income countries face fragmented legacy systems, limited technical capacity, and weak data infrastructure, which makes the ideal full interoperability framework difficult to implement in one step. The guidance lacks a practical gradient implementation path for countries with weak foundational conditions, which may lead to the framework being shelved due to mismatched local conditions.
public.suggestedRevision:
Add the following text to the interoperability and implementation sections:
“For countries with weak digital health foundations and fragmented legacy systems, a phased implementation path is recommended: first achieve basic data interoperability within core public health institutions, then gradually expand to cross-system and cross-regional full interoperability, to ensure the framework is adaptable to local technical and capacity conditions.”
